deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten table of contents for part of the never-written EGA VII on group schemes and abelian schemes. It is written on the back of a typescript page of SGA 4 Exp. VIII §7.9 (points of the étale topos), whose text shows through the paper. The neighbouring pages belong to that SGA 4 typescript, not to the plan.

The planned sections are:

(D) General properties of abelian schemes (proper smooth group schemes with geometrically connected fibres) and of 'pseudo-abelian' schemes. The term is not defined here. It plausibly means a relative analogue of a group with no affine part, or smooth group schemes whose fibres are abelian 'up to' something. The meaning is uncertain.

(E) Extensions of abelian schemes by affine groups, i.e. relative versions of Chevalley's structure theorem: a connected algebraic group over a perfect field is an extension of an abelian variety by a connected linear group. The reading 'Chevalley' is uncertain in the hand.

(D/E?, the letter was overwritten) Torsors under abelian groups, with a later bubble reading roughly 'Groupes abéliens X'. The marginal note '(N'importe où)' means this section can be placed anywhere. It is paired with an 'isotriviality theorem over a field (?)'. Over a field, a torsor under a smooth group (for example an abelian variety) is trivialised by a finite separable extension, so it is isotrivial.

(F) Néron models (?).

A paragraph of 'variations' on the theorem of the square.

References listed:
- SGAD (SGA 3, Schémas en groupes);
- 'BIBLE' (the Chevalley seminar 1956–58, Classification des groupes de Lie algébriques);
- 'Boulder' (probably the 1965 AMS Summer Institute on algebraic groups, Proc. Symp. Pure Math. 9);
- Mumford's book(s): GIT, and Abelian Varieties, then in preparation.

The page contains no mathematics proper, only a list of topics.
errors: No mathematical claims to check. The relative Chevalley structure theorem in (E) fails as stated over imperfect fields and over general bases. That is presumably one reason for the '?' marks and for the term 'pseudo-abélien'.

ideas.what: Chapter on general properties of abelian and 'pseudo-abelian' schemes
ideas.modern_name: Abelian schemes; possibly an analogue of pseudo-abelian varieties (Totaro 2013) or semi-abelian schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (GIT ch. 6), Raynaud, Faltings–Chai; 'pseudo-abelian variety' to Totaro (2013)
ideas.where_published: Abelian schemes appear in SGA 3 and SGA 7 (semi-abelian schemes). 'Pseudo-abélien' for group schemes is not known to me in published Grothendieck texts.

ideas.what: Extensions of abelian schemes by affine group schemes (Chevalley's theorem)
ideas.modern_name: Chevalley structure theorem and its relative versions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Chevalley, Barsotti, Rosenlicht; relative versions Raynaud, Brion, Conrad
ideas.where_published: Partially in SGA 3 and SGA 7 Exp. IX

ideas.what: Torsors under abelian group schemes; isotriviality over a field
ideas.modern_name: Isotriviality of torsors (Lang–Tate; Grothendieck's isotriviality for tori)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 Exp. X (tori); Grothendieck's Bourbaki talks on torsors

ideas.what: Variations on the theorem of the square
ideas.modern_name: Theorem of the square / theorem of the cube for abelian schemes
ideas.where_published: Raynaud, Faisceaux amples (LNM 119) treats this relatively

missed.claim: Grothendieck planned to give 'pseudo-abelian schemes' a place alongside abelian schemes in EGA VII, next to Chevalley-type extension theorems. This predates Totaro's 2013 notion of pseudo-abelian varieties, which was motivated precisely by the failure of Chevalley's theorem over imperfect fields. Whether the meanings coincide cannot be determined from this page.
missed.quote: Propriétés générales des schémas abéliens et pseudo-abéliens
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for the terminology and for the structure theory of algebraic groups over imperfect fields and general bases. It is only a title, though.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a table-of-contents sketch of the planned EGA VII on abelian schemes. Its topics were later covered by SGA 3, SGA 7, Raynaud and Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud. The only slightly notable detail is the early use of the term 'pseudo-abélien', which has no content attached.
transcription_corrections: The page is written on the verso of an SGA 4 Exp. VIII §7.9 typescript; the faint typed text belongs to that typescript, not to the plan.
The third item's circled letter is overwritten (D/E); the item numbering was being revised.
The bubble above the torsor item reads roughly 'Groupes abéliens X'; the last character is uncertain.
The reading 'th. de Chevalley' in (E) is uncertain in the hand.
